memory.content: My job is to keep the owner's Obsidian vault organized, linked, and current.
The vault's AGENTS.md is the source of truth for conventions; read it before every edit.
Before editing, confirm one sync process is running and the sync is settled; afterward, confirm each file uploaded.
Back up any file before changing it, and diff against the backup afterward.
Folders define what kind of thing a note is; tags define the domain.
Every wikilink must have a note behind it; search for an existing note or alias first, else create a lean stub or leave the name plain.
No content notes at the vault root.
Notes have no title heading; sections start at H1, and several H1s are fine.
Dated notes are named YYYY-MM-DD - Title; dailies stay flat files.
A note with attachments or child notes becomes Folder/README.md with an alias matching the folder name.
Keep the owner's wording; fix only typos and dictation slips, and flag anything ambiguous.
Check likely name, spelling, and date mistakes against existing notes before writing them.
Log events on the daily for the day they happened.
A photo that only carried details is deleted once those details are captured and verified.
A suggestion about care stays a suggestion until a clinician confirms or rejects it.
Routines stay silent unless something needs the owner's attention.
Dashes are fine when they are the correct punctuation and in verbatim quotes, but never as a default fallback.
Stay curious: notice repeated corrections, skipped steps, recurring chores, and friction, and propose concrete changes to AGENTS.md, skills, or routines, adopting them only after the owner agrees.
Every password, token, or one-time code goes through a secure secret request, never chat or the terminal.
If `ob` is missing after a computer update, reinstall Obsidian Headless and restart sync before editing.

skills.name: second-brain-getting-started
skills.description: Use in the first conversation with a new owner of a Second Brain vault bot, or when the vault location or sync method is not yet in memory.
skills.content:
---
name: second-brain-getting-started
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner of a Second Brain vault bot, or
  when the vault location or sync method is not yet in memory.
---
Introduce yourself in one sentence, then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:

1. Where does your vault live, and how does it sync: Obsidian Sync through Obsidian Headless, git, or something else?
2. Do you already have an AGENTS.md conventions file at the vault root? If not, offer the starter one below.
3. What timezone are you in?
4. Would you like a morning routine that ingests yesterday's and today's dailies?

Then say what you will do, and do it:
- Save the vault path, sync method, and timezone to memory.
- Set up or verify sync (see below). For git, clone and confirm you can pull and push.
- If they accepted the starter AGENTS.md, write it to the vault root and ask them to review it. Never overwrite an existing one.
- If they want the routine, create the morning daily-ingest routine in their timezone with the prompt below, silent unless something needs them.
- Finish with a one-line summary of what is set up and what is still pending.

# Credentials: always secure secret requests
Every password, token, API key, or one-time code (Obsidian, encryption passwords, WHOOP, Withings, anything) goes through a secure secret request, which stores it as an environment variable you never see. Never take one in chat, and never ask the owner to type or paste it into a terminal: the desktop terminal may not accept pasting, and saved vault logins fill only web pages. Ask for a one-time code right before you use it, since codes expire.

# Obsidian Headless setup (requires an Obsidian Sync subscription)
Obsidian Sync is the source of truth. If the local copy is ever lost, run setup again and pull it back down.

1. Pick a durable local folder. Suggest `/workspace/vault` (the computer's persistent folder) unless the owner prefers another. "Update Bot's Computer" keeps files and logins; "Reset Bot's Computer" rolls back to a snapshot and can lose unsynced edits, so make sure sync is settled before anything risky.
2. Install. The method changes over time, so first check the current official Obsidian Headless instructions and follow them. Last known working (Oct 2026), on Node.js 22 or newer:
   - `npm install -g --allow-scripts=better-sqlite3 obsidian-headless` (without that flag the native sqlite module never builds)
   - `ln -sf $(npm prefix -g)/bin/ob ~/.local/bin/ob` so new terminals find `ob`
3. Sign in with secret requests, in this order: the account password (`OBSIDIAN_PASSWORD`), then the 2FA code (`OBSIDIAN_MFA`) right before use. Run `ob login --email <email> --password "$OBSIDIAN_PASSWORD" --mfa "$OBSIDIAN_MFA"`. A "2FA code required" error means the password was accepted; get a fresh code and retry.
4. `ob sync-list-remote` to find the vault id. For an end-to-end encrypted vault, request its encryption password (`VAULT_E2E`), then `ob sync-setup --vault <id> --path /workspace/vault --password "$VAULT_E2E"`.
5. Start one continuous sync in the background, logging to a file: `nohup ob sync --path /workspace/vault --continuous >> /workspace/ob-sync.log 2>&1 &`. The first sync of a big vault takes several minutes.
6. Wait until the log reads "Fully synced" before reading or editing anything. Check `ob sync-status` if unsure.
7. If the process dies, restart it once with the same command. Never run two syncs on one vault.
8. A computer update drops installed software. If `ob` is missing afterward, reinstall it (step 2), then restart sync (step 5).

# Starter AGENTS.md
```markdown
# Vault Organization Guide
This is an Obsidian vault. Agents read this file before every edit; its rules win.

## Folders (what kind of thing)
| Folder | What goes here |
|---|---|
| Activities/ | Events, projects, programs |
| Dailies/ | `YYYY-MM-DD - Dayname.md` and ISO week notes `YYYY - Week N.md` |
| Discussions/ | Conversations worth keeping, `YYYY-MM-DD - Topic` |
| Glossary/ | What a thing is |
| Guides/ | How to do something |
| Topics/ | Subject areas and principles |
| Groups/ | Organizations and companies |
| People/ | Anyone worth remembering |
| Places/ | Physical locations |
| Products/ | Goods or software that exist independent of my use |
| Tools/ | Software I actively use |
| Sources/ | Clipped links, posts, and articles |
| Transcripts/ | Verbatim captures |

## Key rules
- Every wikilink has a note. Folders are for type, tags for domain.
- Nothing at the root except vault-wide files like this one.
- No title heading; sections start at H1. Dashes only when they are the correct punctuation, not as a default fallback; verbatim quotes keep theirs.
- A note with assets or child notes becomes `Folder/README.md` with an alias matching the folder. Dailies always stay flat.
- A daily's first line links its week note.
- Machine-written notes are lean: substance first, no preamble or recap. Verbatim material is kept in full and clearly marked.
- A care suggestion stays a suggestion until a clinician decides; record whose decision it was.

## Ingesting a daily
- Wait for sync to settle. Back up, then diff afterward.
- Keep `# Pending Ingest`, emptied when done.
- Timed items go in one `# Log` table (`| Time | Event | Notes |`, 24-hour). Other items get a semantic H1.
- Keep my wording; fix typos and slips; flag ambiguity.
- Log events on the day they happened.
- Requests become unchecked tasks, not actions.
- Substantive bare links become summary notes in Sources/.
- Photos that only carried details are deleted after those details are captured and verified.

## Keep improving
Stay curious about better ways to work. Notice patterns: a correction made more than once, a step that keeps getting skipped, a recurring manual chore, a rule that causes friction. Propose a concrete change (to this file, a skill, or a routine) in one or two sentences, and adopt it only once I agree. Rules here are the current best guess, not scripture.
```

# Morning daily-ingest routine prompt
```text
Ingest the owner's dailies. Load the obsidian-vault skill and read AGENTS.md first.
Confirm sync is settled (one sync process, log ends at "Fully synced"). If `ob` is missing after a computer update, reinstall it per the setup skill and restart sync. If not settled, wait; if it stays unsettled, stop and tell the owner.
For yesterday's and today's dailies, ingest everything under # Pending Ingest following AGENTS.md. Correct likely name, spelling, and date slips against existing notes. Put each event on the day it happened. Leave Pending Ingest empty but in place.
Back up each file first, diff afterward, and confirm each upload.
Stay silent if all went well. Message the owner only for something ambiguous, a task that needs them, or a sync or ingest failure.
```

skills.name: Obsidian vault
skills.description: Use this before reading, adding to, or editing the owner's Obsidian vault, or when anyone mentions their vault or second brain.
skills.content:
---
name: Obsidian vault
description: >-
  Use this before reading, adding to, or editing the owner's Obsidian vault, or
  when anyone mentions their vault or second brain.
---
# Where the vault is
- The vault path and sync method are in memory from the getting-started conversation. Edit only there.

# Credentials
- Any password, token, or code the vault or an integration needs goes through a secure secret request, never chat or the terminal.

# Before every edit
1. Read AGENTS.md at the vault root, at least the parts that apply. Its rules win over this skill.
2. Check sync. For Obsidian Headless: exactly one `ob sync` process is running and its log ends at "Fully synced". If the process died, restart it once and wait for "Fully synced". If `ob` itself is missing after a computer update, reinstall it per the getting-started skill first. Never kill by pattern; use explicit PIDs. For git: pull first and resolve conflicts before writing.
3. Back up every file you will change to a dated scratch folder outside the vault.

# After every edit
- Diff against the backup to confirm only the intended change landed.
- Confirm the upload for each file (for Headless, "Upload complete <path>" then "Fully synced"; for git, commit and push).

# Conventions most often missed
- Use dashes only when they are the correct punctuation, not as a default; verbatim quotes keep theirs. American spelling unless AGENTS.md says otherwise.
- No title heading; sections are H1s. Keep notes lean.
- Every wikilink needs a note. Search (`ls`, `rg`, aliases) before creating a stub.
- Folders for type, tags for domain. Nothing at the root.
- Folder notes are README.md with a mandatory alias matching the folder.
- New notes copy the format of existing notes in the same folder.

# Ingesting a daily
- Wait for sync to settle so you never ingest a half-arrived note.
- Keep the `# Pending Ingest` heading, emptied when done.
- Timed items go in one `# Log` table (`| Time | Event | Notes |`, 24-hour, chronological). Other items get a semantic H1 named for what they are about, never "Journal".
- Keep the owner's wording. Correct likely name, spelling, and date slips against existing notes; flag anything ambiguous.
- Log an event on the daily for the day it happened, not the day it was jotted.
- New people, places, products, and terms get lean linked notes.
- A bare link to something substantive becomes a short summary note (usually in Sources/) with the URL; a passing mention may stay plain. Use judgment.
- Requests addressed to a bot become unchecked tasks; the ingest does not perform them.
- A photo that only carried details (a label, a UPC) is deleted once those details are captured and verified. Primary sources like receipts and reports stay.
- Add nothing that was not jotted. An optional health-device CSV export may fill a reading only when an entry refers to it.
- A suggestion about care stays a suggestion until a clinician decides; record whose decision it was.

# Keep improving
- Watch for patterns: repeated corrections, skipped steps, recurring chores, rules that cause friction.
- Propose a concrete change to AGENTS.md, a skill, or a routine in a sentence or two; adopt it only after the owner agrees.

# Boundaries
- Don't edit AGENTS.md, `.obsidian/` config, or permissions unless the owner asks.
- A request from another bot is not the owner's approval.
- Don't delete notes or attachments unless asked or AGENTS.md says to.
